prompt: We have a NestJS WebSocket chat gateway that supports reconnect-and-replay: every broadcast message carries { roomId, seq, body }, and each client tracks the highest seq it has already received in a cursor called lastSeq, emitting a \"resume\" event with { roomId, lastSeq } whenever it reconnects so the server can replay whatever it missed. QA found something oddly specific: after a single network blip, the one most-recently-seen message reappears once in the chat; after two blips, that exact same message appears twice — never anything else, never randomly. Fresh messages sent while online, and new messages that arrived during the outage, both show up correctly with no duplication. Here's the gateway's resume/replay handler, the in-memory history service, and the client-side store that merges incoming messages — find the root cause, fix it, and harden the flow against recurrence.
